subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can rectangular arrays be classified and manipulated to represent information and perform algebraic operations?
in_scope_units: 3.1 Introduction: uses of matrices in mathematics and applications.
3.2 Matrix and Order of a Matrix: entries, rows, columns and notation.
3.3 Types of Matrices and Equality of Matrices.
3.4 Operations on Matrices: addition, scalar multiplication, negatives and differences.
3.5 Multiplication of Matrices and its properties.
3.6 Transpose of a Matrix and transpose properties.
3.7 Symmetric and Skew Symmetric Matrices and decomposition of a square matrix.

known_pitfalls.claim: Matrices can be multiplied entry by entry.
known_pitfalls.correction: Matrix multiplication uses row-by-column products and requires the inner orders to match.
Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative.

known_pitfalls.claim: Equal numbers of elements make matrices equal.
known_pitfalls.correction: Equal matrices must have the same order and equal corresponding entries.
A is symmetric only when A^T=A; it is skew symmetric when A^T=-A.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Example 2 to list possible orders of a matrix with 8 elements.
Use NCERT Example 4 to solve unknown entries from equality of matrices.
Use an Exercise 3.2 problem for matrix addition and scalar multiplication.
Use an Exercise 3.3 problem to compute a conformable matrix product and compare AB with BA.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 3.1 to 3.4 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 3.
